name: On AMD Strix Halo gfx1151, dense 72B models collapse to 4 tok/s due to 256 GB/s LPDDR5X bandwidth while 120B MoE achieves 49 tok/s
symptom: Running large dense models on AMD Strix Halo (Radeon 8060S, 128 GB unified memory) yields low token generation speed despite full GPU offload: Qwen 2.5 72B Q5_K_M runs at only 4.1 tok/s (Q6_K at 3.7 tok/s). However, running GPT-OSS 120B (an MoE model with MXFP4 quantization) on the same machine delivers 49.0 tok/s.
root_cause: Token generation (decode) is memory-bandwidth bound. Strix Halo uses a shared 256-bit LPDDR5X-8000 bus with a peak ceiling of 256 GB/s. For dense 72B models, all ~48-55 GB of weights must be streamed through the bus on every token forward pass (50 GB * 4 tok/s = 200 GB/s, near the bus limit). In contrast, GPT-OSS 120B MoE only activates a small fraction of experts per token and uses MXFP4 microscaling (4-bit), reading only ~4-5 GB of weights per token, enabling 49.0 tok/s within the same 256 GB/s memory bandwidth ceiling.
workaround: For local interactive inference on unified-memory APUs like Strix Halo, deploy Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) architectures (e.g. GPT-OSS 120B) or aggressively quantized models rather than large dense (>70B) models.
notes: Verified by See Hiong on Ryzen AI Max+ 395 (Radeon 8060S, 40 CUs, 128GB LPDDR5X) with llama.cpp b10440 across Qwen 2.5 72B and GPT-OSS 120B.
